assumptions: Anchor is 'center' because the boxes are vehicles viewed from above and the line description states that their centre is the metric position, while bottom_center is the downstream AABB edge rather than wheels.
The exceptions for direction by a police officer or a traffic control signal are left out because that behaviour is not represented by the provided zones, lines, or tracked vehicle events.
The presence of the stop sign and intersection is taken from the binding of stop_zone and stop_line to this approach; the rule does not separately detect a stop sign.
A stop is operationalised as dwelling continuously in stop_zone while still, using max_speed 0.05 as the DSL still threshold.
The statute states no minimum stopped duration, so a 1000 ms still dwell is assumed as evidence of a complete stop rather than slow rolling.
There is no assumed time limit between stopping and crossing stop_line, so BEFORE uses within_ms null.
Direction 'to_right' is the inbound crossing of stop_line, corresponding to movement in the +y direction as described for the line; the statute itself does not state an image direction.
Each tracked vehicle is checked independently and its motion is used as the proxy for its driver, who is not tracked separately.
Under the IMPLIES idiom, a vehicle that never crosses stop_line passes; crossing is the event that triggers the requirement to have stopped first.
Stopping with the vehicle centre in stop_zone, the last 10 metres before the stop line, counts as stopping at the near side at the marked stop line.
raw_output.normalized_explanation: Every vehicle that crosses stop_line inbound must first stop, dwelling still in stop_zone, before that crossing.

provenance.reason: Statute requires a stop but gives no hold duration; 1000 ms of still dwell is the operational threshold assumed to evidence a complete stop.
Statute says 'shall stop' but gives no numeric speed; 0.05 is the DSL threshold supplied for stopped/still.
Statute gives no image direction; line description says inbound vehicles approach from y<0.6 toward y>0.6, and moving downwards (+y) across it is defined as to_right.

text: Unless otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control signal, the driver of a vehicle approaching a stop sign at an intersection shall stop at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line.
